executive_assessment.text: Historical Greater Monrovia evidence locates drainage and flood vulnerabilities at Duala Market in New Kru Town; 2025 crop losses are reported in four named counties.
Land mediation and post-conflict municipal constraints add FCV context. SARTLA and West Point plans remain planned capacity, not proof of resilience or a climate-conflict pathway.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2020 reports: Duala Market in New Kru Town has fragmented, blocked storm drains with no coherent outflow; local discussions report common peak-rainy-season flooding. Wetland-adjacent toilets also pose groundwater-contamination risks.

Source dated 2020 reports: The review says years of conflict left Greater Monrovia's political and administrative authority centrally controlled, limiting fiscal allocation and local governments' ability to provide adequate services.

Source dated 2026-01-09 reports: FAO reports 2025 dry spells after near- or below-average rainfall in May–August, followed by localized flood-related crop losses in Grand Bassa, Margibi, Montserrado and Sinoe counties.
FAO's January 2026 brief describes a 2024–2030 agenda targeting 50,000 hectares of lowland irrigated rice in Lofa, Nimba and Bong; this is a target, not completed irrigation.

UNDP reports Palava Hut hearings in Sanoyea District's Sanoyea Town, Gbonota and Gbonyea heard 52 cases and resolved 51. These historical implementer-reported dispute-resolution outputs are not evaluated climate or reconciliation impacts.

Source dated 2026-05-29 reports: EPA remarks identify farmers in Bong and Lofa, coastal fishers in Grand Cape Mount and Montserrado, and communities in Maryland, Margibi and Nimba as facing rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, coastal erosion and environmental degradation.

Source dated 2026-05-29 reports: The 2025–2030 SARTLA project aims to support climate-smart agriculture, sustainable fisheries, ecosystem restoration, coastal and land management, climate finance, and livelihoods across seven counties, with emphasis on women and youth.

Source dated 2026-03-12 reports: An EPA-implemented, UNDP-supervised and GCF-funded climate-resilience project targets vulnerable West Point, exposed to sea-level rise and intense storms; the ESIA page says the plan includes environmental and social safeguards.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 14 of 15 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The reviewed Liberia sources do not establish a country-specific climate-conflict pathway; none is asserted here.
CCDR flood baseline information is limited beyond Greater Monrovia; its 2024 assessment should not be treated as a current hazard-data inventory.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
No reviewed primary source directly attributes conflict or violence to climate shocks; the post-conflict governance finding is not evidence that climate adaptation is obstructed.
The UNDP ESIA PDF was too large for the reader; only its official publication-page summary is used.
The FAO food-security forecast for June–August 2026 was issued in January 2026; this extraction does not establish what was later realized.
The Greater Monrovia spatial review is a 2020 baseline and the UNDP Palava Hut results are historical implementer-reported achievements; neither should be treated as current 2026 outcome evidence.
SARTLA and West Point adaptation interventions are described as plans or safeguards; no reviewed source provides an independent outcome evaluation.
Current local vulnerability remains incompletely measured. County risk remarks, programme targets and historical municipal capacity diagnoses are not quantified climate-conflict effects.
